PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

To trust means to depend on someone because you believe they will not let you down. In this sub-strand you will learn how Joseph stayed faithful to God and to his master when Potiphar's wife tempted him, how to say No firmly to temptations and to strangers, which people you can trust for your safety, and why Christians put their trust in God always, as Psalm 125:1 teaches.

## Strand 4.0: Christian Values
Sub-strand 4.1: Trust
Suggested lessons: 3

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 4.0 Christian Values, Sub-strand 4.1 Trust
• Genesis 39:1-12, 20-21; Psalm 125:1 (Good News Bible)
• KICD Grade 4 CRE radio programmes 11–13 (protecting yourself from sexual temptations; people you can trust; trusting in God)

PAGE 2: Learning outcomes

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) emulate Joseph by resisting sexual temptations as young people
b) exercise assertiveness in the face of temptations/tempting situations
c) identify people he/she can trust for own safety
d) recite Psalm 125:1 and trust in God always

## Key inquiry questions
1. Whom do you trust at home and school?
2. Why should you avoid talking to strangers?
3. Why should you put your trust in God?

PAGE 3: How we will learn

## Learning experiences
• in turns, read Genesis 39:7-12 and retell the story of Joseph and Potiphar’s wife
• list lessons learnt from the story of Joseph and Potiphar’s wife
• list people they can trust at home, school and in the community
• brainstorm on how to escape/avoid temptations/tempting situations
• in pairs, roleplay saying No! to sexual temptations
• in groups, discuss whom to report to when in danger
• write a poem on, ‘People I trust’
• role-play saying, ‘No’ to strangers to avoid child abuse or kidnap
• list the importance of trusting God
• sing a song about trusting God

## Core competencies
• Self-efficacy: the skill of expressing their needs clearly for help is portrayed as learners list people they can trust at home, school and the community.
• Creativity and Imagination: the skill of coming up with unique and new ideas is exhibited as learners role-play saying, No! to strangers to avoid child abuse or kidnap.

## Values
• Responsibility: learners observe safety precautions as they say No! to strangers.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Developmental Perspective: learners learn how to detect, deter and escape from harmful strangers or relatives.

## Links to other learning areas
• English: the skill of writing is applied as learners write a poem.
• Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners sing a song about trusting God.

PAGE 4: Lesson 1: Joseph and Potiphar's wife

LESSON 1: JOSEPH AND POTIPHAR'S WIFE
====================================

## What you will learn
• Retell the story of Joseph and Potiphar's wife from Genesis 39:7-12.
• List lessons learnt from the story.
• Explain how young people can copy Joseph by keeping away from sexual temptations.

Curriculum outcomes: a) emulate Joseph by resisting sexual temptations as young people

## Introduction
Have you ever been asked to do something you knew was wrong, and the person kept asking again and again? Joseph faced this in Egypt. His answer and his action are a good example for every young Christian.

## Notes

### Who was Joseph?
Joseph was a son of Jacob. His jealous brothers sold him, and he was taken to Egypt. There he was bought by Potiphar, one of the king's officers. The Bible says the LORD was with Joseph and made everything he did succeed. Potiphar saw this, trusted Joseph and put him in charge of his whole house.

PAGE 5: Lesson 1: Joseph and Potiphar's wife — The story (Genesis 39:7-12)

### The story (Genesis 39:7-12)
- Joseph was a young, good-looking man. After some time, Potiphar's wife began to desire him and asked him to sleep with her. This was a sexual temptation.
- Joseph refused. He told her that his master had trusted him with everything in the house except her, because she was his master's wife.
- Joseph asked, "How then could I do such an immoral thing and sin against God?"
- She kept asking him day after day, but he would not listen to her and kept away from her.
- One day Joseph went into the house to do his work and none of the servants was there. She caught him by his robe and asked him again.
- Joseph did not stay to argue. He escaped and ran outside, leaving his robe in her hand.

PAGE 6: Lesson 1: Joseph and Potiphar's wife — Lessons from the story

Later in the chapter she told lies about Joseph and he was put in prison, but the Bible says the LORD was with Joseph there too (Genesis 39:20-21).

### Lessons from the story
- Joseph was faithful to God. He saw the wrong act as sin against God, not only against Potiphar.
- Joseph was trustworthy. He did not betray the master who trusted him.
- He said No clearly, and he kept saying No every time.
- He ran away from the tempting place. Running away from temptation is wise, not cowardly.
- Doing right can sometimes bring trouble, but God stays with those who obey Him.

PAGE 7: Lesson 1: Joseph and Potiphar's wife — Copying Joseph today

### Copying Joseph today
Young people may be tempted by someone who touches them badly, asks them to go to a hidden place, shows them bad pictures or offers gifts in exchange for wrong acts. Like Joseph, you can refuse, move away quickly and tell a trusted adult.

## Key words
• temptation — something that pulls you towards doing wrong
• sexual temptation — being pushed or invited into wrong touching or sexual acts
• trustworthy — a person others can depend on to do right
• emulate — to copy a good example

PAGE 8: Lesson 1: Joseph and Potiphar's wife — Reading and retelling Genesis 39:7-12

## Activity: Reading and retelling Genesis 39:7-12
You will need: Good News Bible or Children's Bible, Exercise book

1. In turns, read Genesis 39:7-12 aloud, one verse per learner.

2. Close the Bible and, as a group, retell the story in the correct order.

3. List on the board the lessons learnt from the story of Joseph and Potiphar's wife.

4. Each learner writes one way he or she will copy Joseph.

## Practice

1. In whose house did Joseph work in Egypt?

2. What did Joseph say when Potiphar's wife tempted him?

3. What did Joseph do when she caught him by his robe?

4. Give two lessons we learn from Joseph.

PAGE 9: Lesson 1: Joseph and Potiphar's wife — Answers to practice

## Answers to practice

1. In the house of Potiphar, one of the king's officers.

2. He refused and asked how he could do such an immoral thing and sin against God.

3. He escaped and ran outside, leaving his robe in her hand.

4. Any two: be faithful to God; be trustworthy; say No clearly; run away from temptation; God is with those who obey Him.

## Summary
• Joseph refused Potiphar's wife because doing wrong would be sin against God.
• He kept saying No and ran away from temptation.
• Young Christians should copy Joseph by keeping away from sexual temptations.

PAGE 10: Lesson 2: Saying No and people we can trust

LESSON 2: SAYING NO AND PEOPLE WE CAN TRUST
===========================================

## What you will learn
• Say No firmly to tempting situations and to strangers.
• Name people they can trust at home, at school and in the community.
• State whom to report to when in danger.

Curriculum outcomes: b) exercise assertiveness in the face of temptations/tempting situations; c) identify people he/she can trust for own safety

## Introduction
A stranger stops you on your way home from school and offers you sweets and a ride. What should you do? Knowing how to say No, and knowing whom to run to, can keep you safe.

PAGE 11: Lesson 2: Saying No and people we can trust — Being assertive

## Notes

### Being assertive
To be assertive means to say clearly and respectfully what you want and what you will not do. An assertive child does not give in just because someone is older, kind, or keeps asking.

Ways to say No firmly:
- Look at the person and say "No!" in a strong, clear voice.
- Do not give long explanations or argue.
- Walk or run away to a safe place where there are people you trust.
- Tell a trusted adult as soon as possible, even if the person told you to keep it a secret.

PAGE 12: Lesson 2: Saying No and people we can trust — Tempting and dangerous situations

### Tempting and dangerous situations
- A stranger offers you gifts, money, sweets or a lift.
- Someone asks you to go with them to a lonely or hidden place.
- Someone touches you in a way that makes you uncomfortable, or asks you to keep touching a secret.
- Someone shows you bad pictures or videos.

You can avoid many of these by walking in groups, going straight home after school, not staying in lonely places, and not accepting gifts from people you do not know.

PAGE 13: Lesson 2: Saying No and people we can trust — People you can trust

### People you can trust
People we can trust are those who care for us and want us to be safe:
- At home: parents, guardians, grandparents, older brothers and sisters who care for you.
- At school: the class teacher, the head teacher, the school nurse.
- In the community: church leaders, Sunday school teachers, police officers, chiefs, and a trusted neighbour your parents know.

Sometimes even a person we know can try to harm us. If anyone, a stranger or a relative, makes you feel unsafe, say No and tell another person you trust.

### Whom to report to when in danger
Report to a parent, guardian, teacher or police officer. In Kenya, children can also call Childline Kenya on 116 free of charge, or the police on 999 or 112.

## Key words
• assertive — able to say clearly and politely what you will or will not do
• stranger — a person you do not know
• report — to tell a responsible person what has happened

PAGE 14: Lesson 2: Saying No and people we can trust — Example 1

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Wanjiku is walking home when a man she does not know says, "Your mother sent me to pick you. Get into my car." What should she do?

Working:
1. She does not know the man, so he is a stranger.
2. Her parents never told her someone would pick her.
3. She should say No firmly, move away to where there are people she trusts, and tell her parent or teacher.

Answer: Say No, do not get into the car, run to a safe place and report to a trusted adult.

PAGE 15: Lesson 2: Saying No and people we can trust — Role-play: Saying No!

## Activity: Role-play: Saying No!
You will need: Paper and pencil

1. In pairs, one learner acts as a stranger offering sweets or a lift; the other says "No!" firmly and walks away.

2. Swap roles and practise saying No to someone who invites you to a hidden place.

3. In groups, list the people you can trust at home, school and in the community, and discuss whom to report to when in danger.

4. Write a short poem titled 'People I trust' and read it to the class.

## Practice

1. What does it mean to be assertive?

2. Name two people you can trust at school.

3. Why should you avoid talking to strangers?

4. What number can a child in Kenya call free to get help?

PAGE 16: Lesson 2: Saying No and people we can trust — Answers to practice

## Answers to practice

1. To say clearly and respectfully what you will or will not do, without giving in.

2. Any two, for example the class teacher, the head teacher, the school nurse.

3. Some strangers may want to harm, abuse or kidnap children, so talking to them or going with them is dangerous.

4. 116 (Childline Kenya).

## Summary
• Say No firmly, move away and tell a trusted adult.
• Trusted people include parents, guardians, teachers, church leaders and police officers.
• Report danger even if someone tells you to keep it a secret.

LESSON 3: TRUSTING IN GOD: PSALM 125:1
======================================

## What you will learn
• Recite Psalm 125:1.
• List reasons why Christians should trust God.
• Show trust in God in daily life.

Curriculum outcomes: d) recite Psalm 125:1 and trust in God always

## Introduction
People can sometimes disappoint us. A friend may forget a promise. But the Bible teaches that God never fails those who depend on Him.

PAGE 17: Lesson 3: Trusting in God: Psalm 125:1 — Psalm 125:1

## Notes

### What is trusting God?
To trust God means to depend on Him completely in everything we do. We believe that He loves us, hears our prayers, and is able to help us.

### Psalm 125:1
The Good News Bible says:

"Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion, which can never be shaken, never be moved."

Mount Zion was the hill in Jerusalem where the Temple stood. A mountain is strong. Wind and rain do not move it. The psalm teaches that a person who trusts God stays strong and steady like that mountain, even when troubles come.

PAGE 18: Lesson 3: Trusting in God: Psalm 125:1 — How we show trust in God

### Why should we trust God?
- God created everything and is in control of all things.
- God loves us and cares for us as a father cares for his children.
- God is always with us, at home, at school and on the way.
- God keeps His promises and never fails.
- When we trust God we are not overcome by fear or worry.
- Joseph trusted God in Egypt, and God was with him in Potiphar's house and even in prison.

### How we show trust in God
- Praying about everything: exams, sickness, safety, needs at home.
- Obeying God's word even when others do wrong.
- Thanking God in good and hard times.
- Asking God for help instead of turning to wrong ways, such as cheating in an examination.
- Singing songs of trust, such as choruses and hymns sung in church.

Trusting God does not mean we stop being careful. We trust God and we also obey the safety rules our parents and teachers give us.

PAGE 19: Lesson 3: Trusting in God: Psalm 125:1 — Reciting and singing about trust

## Key words
• trust — to depend on someone completely
• Mount Zion — the hill in Jerusalem where the Temple stood
• shaken — moved or disturbed

## Activity: Reciting and singing about trust
You will need: Bible, Flash cards

1. Read Psalm 125:1 together, then write it on a flash card.

2. Recite the verse in pairs until each learner can say it without looking.

3. As a class, list the importance of trusting God on the board.

4. Sing a song you know about trusting God.

PAGE 20: Lesson 3: Trusting in God: Psalm 125:1 — Answers to practice

## Practice

1. Recite Psalm 125:1.

2. In Psalm 125:1, what are people who trust God compared to?

3. Give three reasons why Christians should trust God.

## Answers to practice

1. Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion, which can never be shaken, never be moved.

2. Mount Zion, which can never be shaken or moved.

3. Any three: He created and controls everything; He loves and cares for us; He is always with us; He keeps His promises; trusting Him removes fear.

## Summary
• Trusting God means depending on Him completely.
• Psalm 125:1: those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion, never shaken.
• We show trust by praying, obeying and thanking God always.

PAGE 21: Revision quiz

REVISION QUIZ
=============

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Which Bible passage tells the story of Joseph and Potiphar's wife?
   A. Genesis 39:7-12
   B. Exodus 20:12
   C. Psalm 125:1
   D. Acts 7:54-60

2. Why did Joseph refuse Potiphar's wife?
   A. He was afraid of the servants
   B. He did not want to sin against God and betray his master
   C. He wanted to go back home
   D. He was sick

3. What did Joseph leave in the hand of Potiphar's wife when he ran away?
   A. His sandals
   B. His money
   C. His robe
   D. His staff

4. What is the best thing to do when someone tempts you to do a wrong act?
   A. Keep quiet and wait
   B. Say No firmly, move away and tell a trusted adult
   C. Accept so they stop asking
   D. Keep it a secret

5. A stranger offers you sweets and asks you to follow him. What should you do?

6. Which of these is a person you can trust at school?
   A. A stranger at the gate
   B. The class teacher
   C. A person selling sweets outside the fence
   D. Someone you met online

7. Name two people in the community you can report to when in danger.

8. What should you do if a relative touches you in a bad way and tells you to keep it secret?
   A. Keep the secret
   B. Tell another trusted adult
   C. Blame yourself
   D. Run away from home

9. Complete Psalm 125:1: "Those who trust in the LORD are like ______."
   A. a tree by a river
   B. Mount Zion
   C. a strong lion
   D. a shining star

10. Give one reason why we should put our trust in God.

PAGE 22: Quiz answers

ANSWERS
=======

1. A. Genesis 39:7-12
   The story is in Genesis 39:7-12.

2. B. He did not want to sin against God and betray his master
   Joseph asked how he could do such an immoral thing and sin against God.

3. C. His robe
   Genesis 39:12 says he escaped and ran outside, leaving his robe in her hand.

4. B. Say No firmly, move away and tell a trusted adult
   Being assertive means saying No clearly, leaving and reporting.

5. Say No, do not take the sweets, go to a safe place and tell a parent, teacher or other trusted adult.
   Strangers may want to harm or kidnap children.

6. B. The class teacher
   Teachers are responsible for learners' safety at school.

7. Any two, for example a police officer, a chief, a church leader, a trusted neighbour.
   These are responsible people who can help keep children safe.

8. B. Tell another trusted adult
   Anyone who harms you should be reported, even a relative.

9. B. Mount Zion
   The verse compares them to Mount Zion, which can never be shaken.

10. Any one: He created and controls everything; He loves us; He is always with us; He never fails.
   God is faithful and able to help.

### People you can trust
People we can trust are those who care for us and want us to be safe:
- At home: parents, guardians, grandparents, older brothers and sisters who care for you.
- At school: the class teacher, the head teacher, the school nurse.
- In the community: church leaders, Sunday school teachers, police officers, chiefs, and a trusted neighbour your parents know.

Sometimes even a person we know can try to harm us. If anyone, a stranger or a relative, makes you feel unsafe, say No and tell another person you trust.

### Whom to report to when in danger
Report to a parent, guardian, teacher or police officer. In Kenya, children can also call Childline Kenya on 116 free of charge, or the police on 999 or 112.

## Key words
• assertive — able to say clearly and politely what you will or will not do
• stranger — a person you do not know
• report — to tell a responsible person what has happened

studyPages.title: Lesson 2: Saying No and people we can trust — Example 1
studyPages.body:
## Worked examples

### Example 1
Wanjiku is walking home when a man she does not know says, "Your mother sent me to pick you. Get into my car." What should she do?

Working:
1. She does not know the man, so he is a stranger.
2. Her parents never told her someone would pick her.
3. She should say No firmly, move away to where there are people she trusts, and tell her parent or teacher.

Answer: Say No, do not get into the car, run to a safe place and report to a trusted adult.

studyPages.title: Lesson 2: Saying No and people we can trust — Role-play: Saying No!
studyPages.body:
## Activity: Role-play: Saying No!
You will need: Paper and pencil

1. In pairs, one learner acts as a stranger offering sweets or a lift; the other says "No!" firmly and walks away.

2. Swap roles and practise saying No to someone who invites you to a hidden place.

3. In groups, list the people you can trust at home, school and in the community, and discuss whom to report to when in danger.

4. Write a short poem titled 'People I trust' and read it to the class.

## Practice

1. What does it mean to be assertive?

2. Name two people you can trust at school.

3. Why should you avoid talking to strangers?

4. What number can a child in Kenya call free to get help?

studyPages.title: Lesson 2: Saying No and people we can trust — Answers to practice
studyPages.body:
## Answers to practice

1. To say clearly and respectfully what you will or will not do, without giving in.

2. Any two, for example the class teacher, the head teacher, the school nurse.

3. Some strangers may want to harm, abuse or kidnap children, so talking to them or going with them is dangerous.

4. 116 (Childline Kenya).

## Summary
• Say No firmly, move away and tell a trusted adult.
• Trusted people include parents, guardians, teachers, church leaders and police officers.
• Report danger even if someone tells you to keep it a secret.

LESSON 3: TRUSTING IN GOD: PSALM 125:1
======================================

## What you will learn
• Recite Psalm 125:1.
• List reasons why Christians should trust God.
• Show trust in God in daily life.

Curriculum outcomes: d) recite Psalm 125:1 and trust in God always

## Introduction
People can sometimes disappoint us. A friend may forget a promise. But the Bible teaches that God never fails those who depend on Him.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Trusting in God: Psalm 125:1 — Psalm 125:1
studyPages.body:
## Notes

### What is trusting God?
To trust God means to depend on Him completely in everything we do. We believe that He loves us, hears our prayers, and is able to help us.

### Psalm 125:1
The Good News Bible says:

"Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion, which can never be shaken, never be moved."

Mount Zion was the hill in Jerusalem where the Temple stood. A mountain is strong. Wind and rain do not move it. The psalm teaches that a person who trusts God stays strong and steady like that mountain, even when troubles come.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Trusting in God: Psalm 125:1 — How we show trust in God
studyPages.body:
### Why should we trust God?
- God created everything and is in control of all things.
- God loves us and cares for us as a father cares for his children.
- God is always with us, at home, at school and on the way.
- God keeps His promises and never fails.
- When we trust God we are not overcome by fear or worry.
- Joseph trusted God in Egypt, and God was with him in Potiphar's house and even in prison.

### How we show trust in God
- Praying about everything: exams, sickness, safety, needs at home.
- Obeying God's word even when others do wrong.
- Thanking God in good and hard times.
- Asking God for help instead of turning to wrong ways, such as cheating in an examination.
- Singing songs of trust, such as choruses and hymns sung in church.

Trusting God does not mean we stop being careful. We trust God and we also obey the safety rules our parents and teachers give us.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Trusting in God: Psalm 125:1 — Reciting and singing about trust
studyPages.body:
## Key words
• trust — to depend on someone completely
• Mount Zion — the hill in Jerusalem where the Temple stood
• shaken — moved or disturbed

## Activity: Reciting and singing about trust
You will need: Bible, Flash cards

1. Read Psalm 125:1 together, then write it on a flash card.

2. Recite the verse in pairs until each learner can say it without looking.

3. As a class, list the importance of trusting God on the board.

4. Sing a song you know about trusting God.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Trusting in God: Psalm 125:1 — Answers to practice
studyPages.body:
## Practice

1. Recite Psalm 125:1.

2. In Psalm 125:1, what are people who trust God compared to?

3. Give three reasons why Christians should trust God.

## Answers to practice

1. Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion, which can never be shaken, never be moved.

2. Mount Zion, which can never be shaken or moved.

3. Any three: He created and controls everything; He loves and cares for us; He is always with us; He keeps His promises; trusting Him removes fear.

## Summary
• Trusting God means depending on Him completely.
• Psalm 125:1: those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion, never shaken.
• We show trust by praying, obeying and thanking God always.

studyPages.title: Revision quiz
studyPages.body:
REVISION QUIZ
=============

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Which Bible passage tells the story of Joseph and Potiphar's wife?
   A. Genesis 39:7-12
   B. Exodus 20:12
   C. Psalm 125:1
   D. Acts 7:54-60

2. Why did Joseph refuse Potiphar's wife?
   A. He was afraid of the servants
   B. He did not want to sin against God and betray his master
   C. He wanted to go back home
   D. He was sick

3. What did Joseph leave in the hand of Potiphar's wife when he ran away?
   A. His sandals
   B. His money
   C. His robe
   D. His staff

4. What is the best thing to do when someone tempts you to do a wrong act?
   A. Keep quiet and wait
   B. Say No firmly, move away and tell a trusted adult
   C. Accept so they stop asking
   D. Keep it a secret

5. A stranger offers you sweets and asks you to follow him. What should you do?

6. Which of these is a person you can trust at school?
   A. A stranger at the gate
   B. The class teacher
   C. A person selling sweets outside the fence
   D. Someone you met online

7. Name two people in the community you can report to when in danger.

8. What should you do if a relative touches you in a bad way and tells you to keep it secret?
   A. Keep the secret
   B. Tell another trusted adult
   C. Blame yourself
   D. Run away from home

9. Complete Psalm 125:1: "Those who trust in the LORD are like ______."
   A. a tree by a river
   B. Mount Zion
   C. a strong lion
   D. a shining star

10. Give one reason why we should put our trust in God.

studyPages.title: Quiz answers
studyPages.body:
ANSWERS
=======

1. A. Genesis 39:7-12
   The story is in Genesis 39:7-12.

2. B. He did not want to sin against God and betray his master
   Joseph asked how he could do such an immoral thing and sin against God.

3. C. His robe
   Genesis 39:12 says he escaped and ran outside, leaving his robe in her hand.

4. B. Say No firmly, move away and tell a trusted adult
   Being assertive means saying No clearly, leaving and reporting.

5. Say No, do not take the sweets, go to a safe place and tell a parent, teacher or other trusted adult.
   Strangers may want to harm or kidnap children.

6. B. The class teacher
   Teachers are responsible for learners' safety at school.

7. Any two, for example a police officer, a chief, a church leader, a trusted neighbour.
   These are responsible people who can help keep children safe.

8. B. Tell another trusted adult
   Anyone who harms you should be reported, even a relative.

9. B. Mount Zion
   The verse compares them to Mount Zion, which can never be shaken.

10. Any one: He created and controls everything; He loves us; He is always with us; He never fails.
   God is faithful and able to help.
